The '''1978–79 season''' is '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|77th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|48th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
Nineteen days after the death of Santiago Bernabéu, Luis De Carlos was appointed as new President of the club on 21 June 1978.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1978/06/21/deportes/267228016_850215.html|title=Luis De Carlos will be The New Real Madrid Chairman|work=El País|date=22 June 1978|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> The new chairman released a new board of directors on 1 September 1978 in an attempt to normalize the club after the turmoil of last year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1978/09/01/deportes/273448809_850215.html|title=Luis De Carlos appointed a new Board of Directors|work=El País|date=31 August 1978|access-date=2 July 2020|language=Spanish}}</ref> Owing to financial issues including a growing debt, De Carlos did not reinforced the squad with high-profile players, instead of that, there had a few low-cost arrivals such as: [[Rafael García Cortés]] and [[Francisco García Hernández]] along Maté and Hipólito Rincón in a sign of austerity for upcoming years, in an era known as "[[:es:Madrid de los García|The Madrid of Los Garcia]]" until 1982.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/opinion/2019/10/18/5da99d9122601d1b308b4623.html|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=28 October 2019|title=Real Madrid: The Madrid of Los García|language=Spanish|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>

In the [[1978–79 European Cup|European Cup]] the team, shockingly, was eliminated early in the second round by underdogs Swiss side [[Grasshopper Club Zürich]] on the away goals rule.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1978/10/18/deportes/277513202_850215.html|work=El País|date=17 October 1978|access-date=2 July 2020|title=Grasshoppers, an easy rival in Theory, visits Chamartín|language=Spanish}}</ref> Meanwhile, in the [[1978–79 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] the squad advanced to the [[1979 Copa del Rey Final|final]] where it was defeated by [[Valencia CF]] 2–0 at Vicente Calderón Stadium.

The club clinched its 19th League title also second in a row, four points above runners-up [[Sporting Gijón]]. Had they also won the Copa del Rey, Real Madrid would've clinched the [[Double (association football)#Spain|double]], something they would achieve [[1979–80 Real Madrid CF season|next season]].
